intro.label: Quick start
intro.title: Start in three steps
intro.body: Open a terminal in your project's folder, then follow these three steps.

node.title: Check Node
node.body: yokoten runs on Node.js. To see which version you have, type:
node.after: It prints a version number. You need {node} or later. If it prints an older one, or says the command is not found, install Node from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/), then open a new terminal.

run.title: Run yokoten in your project
run.after: It turns on the guard for your AI agent and writes its own files into the project. It changes none of yours.

video.title: Thirty-two seconds on what it does
video.body: An agent, three stops, the first run. Captions in four languages.
video.fallback: Your browser can't play this video here.

next.title: Do what the Next line says
next.body: The first run shows one screen: what it set up, where you are, and the one command to type next. This is a real one:
marks: Something yokoten needs from you. The Fix line under it is the command to run.
`next` is the step you are on; `to do` are the ones after it.
The one command to type now.
next.after: Type the command on the Next line. Then run `npx yokoten` again: it does only what is still missing, and shows the next step. Repeat until the road is done: {stages} stages, {steps} steps in all.
next.more: See every step of the road

stops.title: When your agent gets stopped
stops.body: From now on, yokoten reads the commands your AI agent runs and stops the ones that cannot be undone, such as a force push. The agent is told why and what to do instead, so most stops need nothing from you.
